newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Marines evacuate 1,261 from Freetown.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Marines evacuate 1,261 from Freetown.

text.p: U.S. Marine helicopters staged a third evacuation of foreigners from Sierra Leone on Tuesday, ferrying 1,261 people including 21 Americans to a U.S. warship offshore, Defence Secretary William Cohen said.

Cohen told reporters at a news conference with new British Defence Secretary George Robertson that the evacuees to the USS Kearsarge from the troubled capital, Freetown, included 194 British citizens.

It was the third round of evacuations since Friday from the Freetown to the Kearsarge, which was sent to the West African country's Atlantic coast amid fears of widespread violence after an army coup nine days ago threw out elected President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
Tuesday's evacuation brought to 2,516 the number of persons removed, including 430 Americans, Cohen said.
"The evacuation missions have been safe, fast and efficient. The Marines and the sailors on the Kearsarge have done an outstanding job and I wish to congratualte all of them," he told reporters.
Robertson thanked the United States for aiding in the evacuation of Britons and other foreigners.

Defence officials said Tuesday's evacuees were removed from a beachfront near a restaurant. All U.S. evacuees in last week's operation were taken from Freetown's Mammy Yoko Hotel but that had become too dangerous as an evacuation point.
"We've heard reports of fires and there's been fighting in the area," Pentagon spokeswoman Lt. Col. Nancy Burt said.
CH-53 "Sea Stallion" helicopters, which can carry up to 55 passengers, and CH-46 "Sea Knight" helicopters, capable of carrying 22, have been used in the evacuations.
Washington is encouraging an end to violence and the restoration of democracy in Sierra Leone.
But it has been equivocal about whether it supports military efforts by Nigeria, which with other West African states has hundreds of troops in the country, to overturn the coup and restore Kabbah.
